messages.content: You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

I'm in the kitchen and my husband accidentally slipped while chopping vegetables with a heavy chef's knife. He has a deep, gaping laceration on his forearm. The blood is bright red and it’s bleeding heavily and quickly soaking through the paper towels he's holding against it. What do I do?

Immediately call 911 or emergency services. Have the injured person sit or lie down to prevent fainting. Apply firm, direct pressure to the wound using a clean, heavy cloth or sterile gauze. If the blood soaks through the material, do not remove it; place additional layers of cloth directly on top and continue pressing firmly. If possible and it doesn't cause more pain, elevate the injured arm above the level of his heart. Keep pressure continuous until help arrives.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

We are out at a construction site and a worker just dropped a pane of glass. A large shard sliced into his lower leg. It’s bleeding profusely and pooling on the ground. We have a first aid kit but no medical professionals on site.

Call 911 immediately and inform them of a severe arterial or heavy bleed. Have the worker lie flat. Grab the thickest sterile dressing or clean clothing available and press it as hard as you can directly onto the wound. Do not let go to check the wound. If blood seeps through, stack more dressings on top. If the bleeding is life-threatening, spurting, and cannot be controlled by direct pressure alone, and you have a commercial tourniquet, apply it 2-3 inches above the wound (not on a joint) and note the exact time it was applied.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

I was jogging in the park and found a man lying on the path. He is completely unresponsive when I shake his shoulders and shout, but I can see his chest rising and falling, so he is definitely breathing. He doesn't seem to have any visible bleeding or broken bones.

Call 911 immediately and put them on speakerphone. Since he is breathing but unresponsive, and there is no obvious sign of a spinal injury, carefully roll him onto his side into the recovery position (one arm extended outward, the top leg bent at the knee to stabilize him). Gently tilt his head back slightly to keep his airway open and allow any fluids or vomit to drain. Stay by his side and continuously monitor his breathing until paramedics arrive.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

I went to check on my elderly grandmother in her bedroom. She is slumped over in her chair. I can't wake her up at all, but I hear a snoring sound and her breathing seems steady. She has a history of diabetes and high blood pressure.

Call 911 immediately. Do not attempt to give her anything to eat or drink, including medication or sugar, as she could choke. Check her airway to ensure nothing is blocking it. Gently move her to the floor and place her in the side-lying recovery position to keep her airway clear. Monitor her breathing constantly; if her breathing stops or becomes abnormal (like gasping), roll her onto her back and begin CPR immediately while waiting for EMS.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

I’m at a restaurant with my 55-year-old father. He suddenly stopped eating, turned very pale, and is heavily sweating. He says it feels like an elephant is sitting on his chest and the pain is shooting down his left arm and into his jaw.

Call 911 immediately and state you suspect a heart attack. Have him stop all physical activity, sit down in a comfortable position (often on the floor with knees bent and back supported against a wall), and try to keep him calm. Loosen any tight clothing around his neck or waist. If he is not allergic to aspirin and has no history of internal bleeding, have him chew and swallow one regular adult aspirin (325mg) or four baby aspirins (81mg each). Ask if he has prescribed nitroglycerin and assist him in taking it if he does.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

My wife was out shoveling snow for about twenty minutes. She came inside clutching her chest, looking extremely fatigued. She says she feels a squeezing pressure in the center of her chest and is feeling very nauseous and short of breath.

Call 911 immediately. Women can present with atypical heart attack symptoms, including profound fatigue and nausea, alongside chest pressure. Have her sit down and rest completely; do not let her walk around. Loosen restrictive clothing. If she is not allergic, have her chew an aspirin. Keep her warm and reassure her while waiting for emergency responders. Be prepared to start CPR if she becomes unresponsive and stops breathing.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

We are having a picnic and my 3-year-old toddler was eating a grape. Suddenly he stopped making noise, his eyes went wide, and he is frantically clawing at his throat. His face is starting to turn a slightly blue color and he cannot cough or cry.

This is a severe airway obstruction. Shout for someone to call 911. Immediately stand or kneel behind the child. Wrap your arms around their waist. Make a fist with one hand, place the thumb side just above the child's belly button (well below the breastbone). Grasp your fist with your other hand and give quick, upward abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver). Continue these thrusts forcefully until the grape is expelled and the child can breathe, cough, or cry, or until the child becomes unresponsive.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

I am at a steakhouse and the man at the table next to me just stood up abruptly. He has both hands grasping his neck, he looks terrified, and he isn't making a single sound. He is completely unable to speak or cough.

Ask him loudly, "Are you choking?" If he nods yes and cannot speak, tell him you are going to help. Have someone else call 911. Stand behind him, wrap your arms around his waist, and locate his navel. Place the thumb side of your fist just above the navel, grab your fist with your other hand, and perform hard, rapid, inward and upward abdominal thrusts. Continue until the blockage is dislodged or he loses consciousness.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

I was boiling a large pot of pasta water and accidentally spilled the boiling water directly onto my bare forearm. The skin is bright red, intensely painful, and large blisters are already starting to form.

Immediately remove any jewelry or restrictive clothing near the burn before swelling occurs. Run cool (not ice cold) tap water over the burn for at least 10 to 20 minutes to stop the burning process. Do not apply ice, butter, or ointments, and do not pop the blisters. After cooling, loosely cover the burn with a sterile, non-stick dressing or a clean, lint-free cloth like a pillowcase. Seek medical evaluation, as blistering indicates a second-degree burn.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

My friend accidentally backed his bare calf into the hot exhaust pipe of a running motorcycle. The burn mark is white, charred, and leathery, but surprisingly he says it doesn't hurt as much as it looks like it should.

The lack of pain and charred appearance indicates a severe, third-degree burn where nerve endings have been damaged. Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room immediately. Do not try to clean the burn or remove any clothing that might be stuck to the melted skin. Cool the area briefly with cool water, but avoid prolonged cooling as it can cause hypothermia with severe burns. Cover the area loosely with a dry, sterile bandage or clean cloth to prevent infection.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

A coworker in my office just collapsed out of his chair. He is on the floor, unconscious, and his entire body is violently convulsing. He has knocked over a chair and is close to a glass coffee table.

Do not try to hold him down or stop his movements, and never put anything in his mouth. Immediately clear the area of hard or sharp objects (like the chair and glass table) to prevent injury. Slip something soft, like a folded jacket or cushion, under his head. Note the time the seizure started. If the seizure lasts longer than 5 minutes, if he has difficulty breathing afterward, or if he doesn't regain consciousness, call 911. Once the shaking stops, gently roll him onto his side into the recovery position.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

I am on the subway and a teenage girl suddenly dropped to the floor. Her eyes rolled back, and she is having rhythmic, jerking movements of her arms and legs. Foam is starting to form at the corner of her mouth.

Protect her from injury by guiding her to the floor if she is falling, and clear away any hazards. Place a soft item under her head. Do not restrain her or attempt to pry her mouth open. Time the seizure. Once the convulsing stops, carefully roll her onto her side (recovery position) to allow the saliva/foam to drain and keep her airway clear. Stay with her and comfort her as she regains awareness. Call 911 since this occurred in a public setting and her medical history is unknown.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

My son was skateboarding and fell hard on his outstretched hand. He is screaming in pain. His forearm is swelling rapidly and there is a very obvious, unnatural bend in the middle of his arm where there shouldn't be a joint.

Call 911 or take him to the emergency room immediately. Do not attempt to straighten the arm or push any bones back into place. Keep the arm as completely still as possible. You can create a makeshift splint using a rolled-up magazine, rigid cardboard, or a towel, gently securing it above and below the injury without tying it too tight. Apply a cold pack wrapped in a cloth to the area to help with swelling and pain, but do not place ice directly on the skin.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

We were hiking on a rocky trail and my partner slipped. He heard a loud snap. He cannot put any weight on his leg, and tearing through his hiking pants, I can see a piece of bone protruding through the skin. It is bleeding.

This is an open fracture; call 911 immediately. Do not try to realign the leg or push the bone back in. Control the bleeding by applying gentle pressure around the edges of the wound with a clean cloth or sterile dressing, being careful not to press directly on the exposed bone. Cover the wound with a sterile dressing to prevent infection. Keep him completely still, warm, and reassure him to help prevent shock while waiting for mountain rescue or paramedics.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

My 80-year-old grandfather has been sick for two days. Today, his temperature is reading 103.5°F. He is extremely lethargic, doesn't know what day it is, and is muttering things that don't make sense. His skin feels hot and dry.

Call 911 or get him to an emergency room immediately. High fever combined with sudden confusion or altered mental status in an elderly person is a medical emergency and could indicate a severe infection like sepsis or pneumonia. Do not leave him alone. Help him cool down by removing excess clothing and applying cool, damp washcloths to his forehead, neck, and armpits. Do not force him to drink fluids if he is too confused, as he might choke.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

My 5-year-old daughter had a mild cold yesterday, but this afternoon she suddenly spiked a fever of 104°F. She won't answer my questions, is staring blankly, and seems too weak to even lift her head off the pillow.

Seek immediate emergency medical care (call 911 or go to the ER). A sudden high fever accompanied by severe lethargy, unresponsiveness, or a blank stare in a child requires urgent evaluation to rule out serious conditions like meningitis. Dress her in lightweight clothing and sponge her with lukewarm (not cold) water to gently lower her temperature. Do not give her aspirin. Monitor her breathing closely on the way to the hospital.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

My friend and I were eating at a bakery. She had a bite of a cookie and immediately started coughing. Now, five minutes later, her lips and eyelids are swelling massively, she has hives all over her neck, and she says her throat feels "tight."

This is anaphylaxis, a severe and potentially life-threatening allergic reaction. Call 911 immediately. Ask her if she carries an epinephrine auto-injector (EpiPen) and assist her in using it immediately by firmly pressing it into the outer middle of her thigh. Have her sit down in a comfortable position to help her breathe. If she feels dizzy or faint, have her lie flat with her legs elevated. Do not wait to see if an antihistamine will work; epinephrine is required.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

We are on a remote camping trip and my husband got stung by a wasp. He is highly allergic. He forgot his EpiPen. He is wheezing loudly, struggling to catch his breath, and his face is visibly swelling.

Call 911 or emergency services immediately and emphasize that this is a severe allergic reaction without an EpiPen available. Keep him as calm as possible, as panic will worsen his breathing. Have him sit in an upright, leaning-forward position to maximize his airway. If you have an over-the-counter oral antihistamine (like Benadryl), give it to him immediately, provided he can swallow safely without choking. Dispatch may guide you on further interim steps while help is en route.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

During a stressful exam, my classmate started breathing very rapidly and shallowly. She is clutching her chest, gasping for air, and making a high-pitched wheezing sound every time she exhales. She has a known history of asthma.

Remain calm and help her sit upright, which makes breathing easier. Ask her where her rescue inhaler (albuterol) is and help her retrieve it. Shake the inhaler, and have her take 1 to 2 puffs, ideally using a spacer if she has one. Encourage her to take slow, deep breaths, breathing in through the nose and out through pursed lips. If her breathing does not improve within 5 to 10 minutes after using the inhaler, or if her lips start turning blue, call 911 immediately.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

My mother just got off a 12-hour international flight. While walking through the airport, she suddenly grabbed her chest, gasped for air, and collapsed into a chair. She says she physically cannot get enough air into her lungs and her heart is racing.

Call 911 immediately. Sudden, severe shortness of breath after prolonged immobility (like a long flight) is a major red flag for a pulmonary embolism (a blood clot in the lungs). Have her remain sitting up if that is most comfortable for her breathing. Do not let her walk or exert herself in any way. Keep her calm and loosen any tight clothing. Stay with her and be prepared to perform CPR if she loses consciousness and stops breathing.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
We are at a remote campsite and my friend was chopping firewood. The axe glanced off the log and deeply gashed his shin. It's bleeding heavily and won't stop with normal pressure.

Call emergency services immediately. Have him lie down. Apply direct, firm pressure with the cleanest thick cloth available. If blood soaks through, add more layers—do not remove the original cloth. If heavy bleeding continues despite direct pressure, and a tourniquet is available, apply it 2-3 inches above the wound (not on a joint) and note the time.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

I just witnessed a minor car collision. The passenger bumped her head against the side window. She has a deep laceration on her scalp and it is bleeding profusely, covering her face and shirt. She is conscious but dazed.

Call 911. Head wounds bleed heavily due to dense blood vessels. Have her sit down and lean slightly forward so blood doesn't drain into her airway. Apply firm, direct pressure to the cut with a clean cloth or sterile dressing. Keep her still and talking to monitor her consciousness until help arrives. Do not press hard if you suspect a skull fracture.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
My son has been playing soccer in 95-degree heat. He complained of dizziness, stopped sweating, and then suddenly collapsed on the field. He is breathing but completely unresponsive.

Call 911 immediately; this is likely heat stroke, a life-threatening emergency. Move him to shade immediately. Cool him rapidly by whatever means available: douse him with cold water, apply ice packs to his neck, armpits, and groin, and fan him vigorously. Place him in the recovery position on his side while monitoring his breathing.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

I'm at a college party and found a student passed out on a couch. There are empty liquor bottles around him. I can't wake him up by shouting or shaking him. His breathing is very slow and shallow, maybe 6 breaths a minute.

Call 911 immediately for suspected alcohol poisoning. Do not assume he will "sleep it off." Roll him onto his side into the recovery position to prevent choking if he vomits. Stay with him and continuously monitor his breathing. If his breathing stops completely, roll him onto his back and begin CPR.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

My 70-year-old neighbor was gardening. She suddenly sat down, clutching her chest. She says she feels a heavy, crushing pain, and she's sweating profusely and looks extremely anxious, saying she feels like something terrible is going to happen.

Call 911 immediately and report a suspected heart attack. Keep her seated and rested; do not let her walk. Loosen tight clothing. If she is not allergic, have her chew one regular adult aspirin (325mg). Keep her calm and wait for paramedics. Be ready to start CPR if she loses consciousness.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
During a little league baseball game, a batter was struck squarely in the chest by a fast pitch. He took two steps and collapsed. He is not moving, and when I check his chest, he is not breathing.

Call 911 immediately. This may be commotio cordis, where a sudden impact causes cardiac arrest. Yell for an AED (Automated External Defibrillator). Begin CPR immediately, starting with chest compressions (push hard and fast in the center of the chest). Use the AED as soon as it arrives, following its voice prompts.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

I am at a nursing home visiting my grandfather. The man at the next table is eating a piece of tough meat, starts gagging, and then goes completely silent. He is clawing at his throat, wide-eyed, and cannot cough.

Ask "Are you choking?" If he nods, have someone call 911. Stand behind him, wrap your arms around his waist. Place the thumb side of your fist just above his navel, grab your fist with your other hand, and give quick, forceful upward thrusts (Heimlich maneuver) until the object is dislodged.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
My sister is 8 months pregnant. We were eating dinner and she suddenly started choking. She cannot breathe or speak, and her face is turning red. I know I shouldn't press on her belly.

Have someone call 911. Stand behind her and wrap your arms under her armpits, placing your hands on the lower half of her breastbone (chest thrusts, not abdominal thrusts). Make a fist with one hand, grab it with the other, and pull straight back with quick, firm thrusts until the airway clears.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
I am in the chemistry lab and my partner accidentally splashed a high-concentration acid onto her forearm. Her skin is immediately blistering and she is screaming in pain.

Direct her to the emergency safety shower or nearest sink immediately. Flush the area with copious amounts of cool, running water for at least 20 minutes. Have someone call 911. While rinsing, carefully remove any contaminated clothing or jewelry near the burn. Do not apply any neutralizing agents, creams, or bandages until thoroughly rinsed.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

My toddler was playing behind the TV and chewed on an plugged-in electrical cord. He got a shock, cried out, and dropped it. He has a charred, white burn mark on his lip and corner of his mouth. He seems okay now but is crying.

Call 911 or go to the emergency room immediately. Electrical burns can cause severe internal tissue damage and cardiac arrhythmias that aren't immediately visible. Ensure the power source is off before touching him. Do not apply ice or ointments to the burn. Cover it loosely with a dry, sterile dressing.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
My 18-month-old baby has had a fever all day. Suddenly, his eyes rolled back and his arms and legs started twitching violently. He isn't responding to my voice.

This is likely a febrile seizure. Call 911. Do not restrain him or put anything in his mouth. Place him on the floor away from hard objects. Loosen tight clothing, especially around the neck. Note the time the seizure started. Once the twitching stops, roll him onto his side to keep his airway clear.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
My pregnant wife (third trimester) complained of a severe headache and visual spots. Suddenly, she collapsed and is having a full-body seizure on the living room floor.

Call 911 immediately; this is a life-threatening obstetric emergency (eclampsia). Do not restrain her or put anything in her mouth. Move furniture away to prevent injury. Place a pillow or folded clothing under her head. Once the seizure stops, roll her onto her left side to improve blood flow to her and the baby, and monitor breathing.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
At the warehouse, a heavy pallet fell and pinned my coworker's lower leg. We used a forklift to get it off him. His leg is severely mangled, bleeding, and he is screaming in agony.

Call 911 immediately. Do not attempt to move the leg or realign it. Stop any severe bleeding by applying direct pressure around the wound, or use a tourniquet if bleeding is life-threatening and cannot be controlled. Keep him still and cover him with a coat or blanket to treat for shock.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
My elderly mother slipped on an icy step. She is on the ground, unable to get up, and complaining of severe pain in her right hip. Her right leg appears shorter than the left and is turned outward.

Call 911. Do not try to help her stand or move her, as this indicates a likely hip or femur fracture. Keep her exactly where she is. Keep her warm with blankets to prevent shock. Reassure her and wait for paramedics to properly immobilize her before moving.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
My newborn baby is only 4 weeks old. She feels very warm, and when I took her rectal temperature, it read 101.2°F. She is crying weakly and refusing to nurse.

Go to the nearest pediatric emergency room immediately or call 911. Any fever (100.4°F or higher) in an infant under 3 months old is a medical emergency that requires a full workup for serious bacterial infection. Do not give her Tylenol or any fever-reducing medication before seeing a doctor.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
My roommate has had a high fever (103°F) since yesterday. Today, he is vomiting, incredibly sensitive to the light in the room, and says his neck is so stiff he cannot touch his chin to his chest.

Call 911 or go to the emergency room immediately. A high fever combined with a stiff neck, severe headache, and light sensitivity are classic signs of meningitis, a critical emergency. Keep him quiet and lower the lights. Do not wait to see if symptoms improve.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
I'm a teacher. A student ate a cookie from a classmate. Within minutes, he started coughing, his face is swelling, and he's breaking out in hives. He doesn't have an EpiPen on file at the school.

Call 911 immediately and declare an anaphylactic emergency. Send someone to get the school's stock epinephrine auto-injector if available. Keep the child seated upright to help with breathing. Do not give them anything by mouth except an oral antihistamine if directed by dispatch/protocols. Monitor breathing closely.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
I just took my first dose of a newly prescribed antibiotic. Twenty minutes later, my throat feels incredibly tight, my lips are tingling and swelling, and I feel dizzy and lightheaded.

Call 911 immediately. This is a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) to the medication. If you have an epinephrine auto-injector from a previous allergy, use it now. Lie down flat on your back and elevate your legs to help with blood flow and dizziness. Unlock your front door if possible so paramedics can enter.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
We just pulled a teenager out of the swimming pool. He was underwater for an unknown amount of time. He is unconscious, his lips are blue, but he just let out a sputtering gasp for air.

Call 911 immediately. Even though he gasped, he needs immediate oxygen and medical evaluation to prevent secondary drowning. Place him in the recovery position (on his side) to allow water and vomit to drain from his airway. Monitor his breathing constantly; if he stops breathing, roll him onto his back and start CPR immediately.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
My neighbor escaped from a house fire. He doesn't have any visible burns on his skin, but his voice is hoarse, he is coughing up dark soot, and he is struggling to take a deep breath.

Call 911 immediately. Smoke inhalation can cause severe internal swelling of the airway and chemical damage to the lungs, even without external burns. Keep him sitting upright to ease breathing. Keep him calm and do not let him walk or exert himself. Wait for EMS to administer high-flow oxygen.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
My neighbor was cutting branches with a chainsaw and it kicked back, deeply slicing his upper thigh. Blood is spurting out in bright red pulses.

Call 911 immediately. This is a life-threatening arterial bleed. Have him lie flat. If you have a commercial tourniquet, apply it "high and tight" on the leg above the wound immediately. If no tourniquet is available, pack the wound with clean cloth and apply massive, sustained body-weight pressure directly onto the wound. Do not release pressure.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
I found my roommate unresponsive on his bed with a syringe nearby. His lips are blue, and he is taking a very shallow, gurgling breath only every 10 seconds or so.

Call 911 and report a suspected opioid overdose. Administer Naloxone (Narcan) immediately if you have it (spray into one nostril). Roll him onto his back. Because his breathing is dangerously slow, begin rescue breathing or CPR (compressions) until he breathes normally or EMS arrives.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
My husband was jogging and had to stop. He is clutching his chest, looks pale, and says he feels a tight squeezing in his chest that moves up into his jaw. He has a prescription for nitroglycerin.

Call 911. Have him sit down and rest. Assist him in taking his prescribed nitroglycerin (usually one tablet under the tongue). If the pain does not subside after 5 minutes, assist with a second dose if prescribed. Have him chew an adult aspirin if he isn't allergic. Keep him calm.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

An elderly man at the nursing home where I work swallowed a large pill and suddenly grabbed his throat. He is conscious, wide-eyed, and completely unable to make a sound or breathe. He is in a wheelchair.

Call 911. Lock the wheelchair brakes. If you cannot get your arms around him effectively in the chair, or if he is too frail for abdominal thrusts, perform chest thrusts. Place your arms under his armpits, make a fist over the lower half of his breastbone, and pull straight back forcefully until the pill is dislodged.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
I was unclogging a drain and the liquid lye splashed up directly into my right eye. It burns intensely and I can barely open it.

Immediately flush the eye with continuously running, lukewarm tap water. Hold the eyelid open and flush from the bridge of the nose outward so the chemical doesn't wash into the other eye. Have someone call 911 or Poison Control. Continue flushing for at least 15-20 minutes uninterrupted.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
My epileptic friend just started having a grand mal seizure in the middle of a grocery store aisle. Her limbs are jerking and she hit her head on a shelf on the way down.

Clear the aisle of carts and hard objects. Place a folded jacket under her head to protect it from further injury. Do not restrain her or put anything in her mouth. Time the seizure. Since she hit her head, call 911. Once the jerking stops, roll her onto her side into the recovery position.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
My daughter fell off the monkey bars. She is cradling her left arm against her chest and her shoulder looks severely dropped. There is a visible, painful lump right on her collarbone.

Call 911 or take her to the emergency room. Do not attempt to push the bone back or move her arm. Support the arm in the position she is holding it. You can create a makeshift sling using a triangular bandage or a shirt to keep the arm still and take the weight off the collarbone. Apply a cold pack over a cloth to the area.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
We are hiking in the desert. My friend stopped sweating an hour ago. Now, he is stumbling, slurring his words, and his skin is blazing hot and completely dry to the touch.

Call 911 immediately; this is heat stroke, a fatal condition if untreated. Move him to whatever shade is available. Rapidly cool him by dousing him with water and fanning him vigorously. Do not give him fluids to drink as his altered mental state makes choking a high risk.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.

My son has a known peanut allergy. He accidentally ate a contaminated brownie. We used his EpiPen 15 minutes ago and his breathing improved, but now his wheezing is coming back and he says he feels dizzy.

Call 911 immediately and inform them of a biphasic anaphylactic reaction. If you have a second EpiPen, administer it now in the outer thigh. Have him lie flat with his legs elevated to combat the dizziness and drop in blood pressure. Keep him calm until paramedics arrive.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
My father has COPD and is on home oxygen. He suddenly started gasping for air, leaning forward with his hands on his knees, and his lips are taking on a bluish tint. His rescue inhaler isn't helping.

Call 911 immediately. Ensure his oxygen tubing is connected and flowing correctly, but do not arbitrarily increase the flow rate beyond his prescription without medical guidance. Keep him in the "tripod" position (leaning forward), which maximizes lung capacity. Keep him calm and encourage pursed-lip breathing.
You are an expert emergency medical dispatcher. Provide a concise, direct diagnosis and immediate action steps with no filler.
My coworker was using a table saw and accidentally severed his index and middle fingers completely. His hand is bleeding profusely.

Call 911. Apply firm, direct pressure to the bleeding hand with sterile gauze or a clean cloth. Elevate the hand. Have someone else locate the severed digits. Gently rinse the digits with clean water (do not scrub), wrap them in damp gauze, place them in a sealed plastic bag, and put that bag in a container of ice water. Do not put the digits directly on ice.
